first_impression.reaction: Searched 'wedding table settings' on a Sunday, mostly to see what goes where before we start saving Pinterest boards. The intro is calm and grown-up, no 'dream day' anywhere, and the line about a venue's cupboards not matching the look we fall for is the hook for us, because we haven't even picked a country yet. I skimmed the etiquette (useful, if a bit Emily Post 101), skimmed the themes, and read the destination section and the trial-table checklist properly. It's a good reference page. It's not the page that makes us enquire, but it doesn't put us off either.

journey.quote: For a wedding abroad, it also sets out what to ask the venue before you fall for a look its cupboards cannot deliver.
journey.reaction: That's the one line that tells me this isn't just another listicle of pretty tables. It's exactly the trap we'd fall into overseas.

journey.section: The place setting, piece by piece
journey.quote: Treat them as a well-tested framework rather than a set of Australian rules, and adapt them to your menu.
journey.reaction: Honest about where the rules come from. I like that it doesn't pretend to be the authority.

journey.quote: This is why the setting cannot be finalised until the menu is. A late soup or sorbet course changes every place at every table.
journey.reaction: Practical, the kind of knock-on effect I wouldn't have thought about. Good to know the order of decisions.

journey.section: Glassware, in the order it is used
journey.quote: If your drinks list runs to several wines, count the glasses before you choose a low, wide centrepiece, because both need the same strip of table.
journey.reaction: Real insider detail. James will actually care about this one because he'll want the wine list.

journey.quote: A theme is carried by the finish of each piece, not by adding more to the table.
journey.reaction: Agree completely. Restraint is what stops it looking try-hard.

journey.quote: - **Stationery:** kraft or cotton card, or names painted onto a leaf or a slice of timber.
journey.reaction: Names painted on a slice of timber is the rustic-barn look our friends would quietly laugh at. Undercuts the 'not adding more' line just above.
Not for us, but fair enough as an option. Skimmed past.

journey.section: Table settings for a destination wedding
journey.quote: Whatever tableware a venue holds decides how far a theme can go before pieces need to be hired in. Ask these questions early, and ask for the answers in writing.
journey.reaction: This is the useful part for us. 'In writing' speaks to my hidden-costs fear.

journey.section: Table settings for a destination wedding
journey.quote: Which pieces would need to be hired in for our theme and guest count?
journey.reaction: Good question, but the obvious follow-up is what that hire adds to the bill. That's where the surprise cost hides, and the list doesn't prompt us to ask it.

journey.section: Table settings for a destination wedding
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms inclusions in writing before you commit, so the setting you approve is the setting your guests sit down to.
journey.reaction: Reassuring and specific. This is the kind of accountability line I'm looking for.

journey.section: What to check at the trial table
journey.quote: At a wedding abroad, ask for clear photos or a video walk-through if you cannot be there.
journey.reaction: So we'd be squinting at a video from Sydney and judging the table ourselves? That's the spreadsheet-evenings scenario we want to avoid. Who looks at it with us?

journey.section: What to check at the trial table
journey.quote: **Sightlines.** Sit down. Can you see and speak to the guest opposite?
journey.reaction: Simple and sensible. Nice that it's about guests, not just looks.

journey.quote: To keep the seating plan and name cards in one place, [plan seating and name cards in Wonderland Studio]
journey.reaction: What is Wonderland Studio? A tool, a person, a paid add-on? Not explained, so I probably wouldn't click.

journey.section: Set the table with someone in your corner
journey.quote: With one Wedded Advisor, start to finish, as a single point of contact, the questions to the venue, the mock-up and the final setting sit with one person who knows your plans.
journey.reaction: Better than most, because it names the actual tasks. Still the 'start to finish' line every planner uses. Who is physically at the venue on the day?

unanswered_questions: When pieces have to be hired in abroad, how do we see what that adds to the quote before we commit?
If we can't fly over for the mock-up, does our Wedded Advisor review the photos or video with us, or is that on us?
What is Wonderland Studio: a free planning tool, a paid service, or something else?
Is there a real wedding (venue, date) where we can see one of these settings actually laid overseas?
Who is on the ground at the venue on the day to check the tables are set as approved? (deferred business detail)
Does Wedded Wonderland source and vet the hire company and stylist, or do we? (deferred business detail)
How does Wedded Wonderland charge for this: flat fee, percentage or commission on hire? (deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: - **Stationery:** kraft or cotton card, or names painted onto a leaf or a slice of timber.
turn_offs_found.why: Reads as the rustic-craft cliché. Our fear is looking try-hard to our friends, and this is the detail they'd screenshot.

turn_offs_found.quote: With one Wedded Advisor, start to finish, as a single point of contact, the questions to the venue, the mock-up and the final setting sit with one person who knows your plans.
turn_offs_found.why: 'Start to finish' is the end-to-end claim every planner makes. It's softened by naming the tasks, but it still doesn't say who is accountable at the venue on the day.

would_share_with: James: the glassware section and the trial-table checklist, because he'll own the wine list and the sightlines point
Mum: the 'Table settings for a destination wedding' question list, because she'll want to know we'd ask the right things before booking anywhere

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready to talk through your reception, speak with our [Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=22-amazing-table-settings-for-every-wedding-theme&utm_content=closing) team.
cta_reaction.why: Not pushy, which I appreciate, but we're 14 months out with no destination. Table settings is a month-ten problem. I'd bookmark the page, not enquire from it. A real overseas wedding linked here would make me look further.

top_3_changes: Prompt the hidden-cost question in the destination list. Old: "- Which pieces would need to be hired in for our theme and guest count?" New: "- Which pieces would need to be hired in for our theme and guest count, and what would that add to the quote?"

Don't leave the remote mock-up on us. Old: "At a wedding abroad, ask for clear photos or a video walk-through if you cannot be there." New: "At a wedding abroad, ask for clear photos or a video walk-through if you cannot be there, and go through them with your Wedded Advisor." (Consistent with the closing, which already says the mock-up sits with the Advisor.)
Cut the try-hard rustic option. Old: "- **Stationery:** kraft or cotton card, or names painted onto a leaf or a slice of timber." New: "- **Stationery:** kraft or cotton card in a warm tone."

Journey types and severities limited to schema enums

No invented brand facts; fees, commissions, sourcing and vetting of suppliers and hire, and on-the-ground staffing listed as deferred unanswered questions
Suggested edits use exact old/new strings and add no new facts or measurements
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots) ignored

open_questions.question: Wonderland Studio is linked without explanation. Can the anchor or surrounding sentence say what it is (tool or service) using an approved brand description?
Is there a real overseas Wedded Wonderland wedding (venue, date) that could be linked from the destination section as a trust signal?

assumptions: Sophie & James arrived via a Google search for 'wedding table settings' at the early-research stage with no destination chosen, so relevance is 3 and enquiry likelihood 2 (they enquire after 2 to 3 posts plus a real wedding).
Fees, commissions, supplier and hire sourcing and vetting are deferred by the brand and are raised only as unanswered questions, not as must-fix.
Fast-mode read: read the intro, glassware, destination section, trial-table checklist and close in full; skimmed etiquette detail, theme lists and FAQ.
